narrative: OMX30 enters Monday with tailwinds from continental Europe's strong opens (DAX +153bp, CAC +65bp), supported by a +0.596% weighted correlation signal and falling yields (US 10Y -51bp to 4.679%) that ease refinancing pressure. The index sits deeply bullish structurally—+8.1% above the 200-MA, MACD above signal with +3.225 histogram, and 90-day momentum at +7.0%—but is flashing caution flags: Stochastic K at 97.2 indicates overbought conditions, ADX weakness (6.4) means trend strength is fragile, and the index sits 99% of its 52-week range with only -0.2% from all-time highs. Oil's -7.26% decline is positive for cost-sensitive industrials, while copper strength (+0.89%) and gold appreciation (+0.67%) directly support cyclical mining. Expect a cautious +0.3%–+0.7% open, but mean-reversion risk is material given crowded technicals.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens with structural uptrend intact but overbought on intraday timeframes. DAX/CAC momentum is contagious, but weak ADX (6.4) means trend is fragile—treat any +0.5% gap-up with skepticism. Key support: 3085 (lower Bollinger band); resistance: 3180 (50-MA). Watch for profit-taking in names that have rallied hard into overbought RSI territory. Industrials (28% weighting) likely to lead—Volvo and Atlas Copco benefit from oil cost relief and maintained momentum; hedge with defensive names (AstraZeneca, Essity) if risk appetite cracks. Boliden is a core long on copper+gold tailwinds. Banks (18%) may see modest NIM lift from stable-to-lower yields, but refinancing relief is priced in. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is only material catalyst today; any miss would test 3123 pivot downward fast given elevated technicals. Skew trades toward tactical longs on dips rather than chasing rallies.
